explanation: The change rewrites the pipe check in `requiresInlineTypeCheckBlock` from `!checkIfClassIsExported(pipeRef.node)` to `!env.canReferenceType(pipeRef)`, a strictly stronger test (it also rejects classes that cannot be imported from the TCB environment, e.g. outside `rootDir`). The caller in context.ts still passes `pipes` — the map of every pipe in the component's scope — even though the parameter is named `usedPipes`. The fix message explicitly blames this change (#46096) and the fix builds a list from `boundTarget.getUsedPipes()` and passes only those, confirming the ground truth's mechanism. One caveat worth noting: iterating over all in-scope pipes rather than only used ones pre-existed this change; the change only made that latent over-approximation harmful by tightening the predicate, so it is a 'regression exposed by altering the faulty line' rather than a brand-new mistake. A reviewer could see `pipes` being passed to a parameter called `usedPipes` in the diff, but would need outside knowledge that `pipes` is the whole scope map and that `canReferenceType` is much stricter than the export check to realize the impact, hence 'partly'.

The change itself swaps `bootstrapDone.complete()` for `bootstrapDone.unsubscribe()` inside the new `if (!bootstrapDone.closed)` guard. In RxJS, `Subject.unsubscribe()` marks the subject closed and drops its observers but never sends a `complete` notification to them, so anything waiting for `bootstrapDone` to complete (the enabledBlocking initial navigation in `navigation_transition.ts`) hangs and its `finalize` never clears `currentNavigation`. The fix confirms this mechanism: it re-adds `bootstrapDone.complete()` before `unsubscribe()` and adds a defensive `take(1)` in the transition pipeline, matching the fix message ('completes the `bootstrapDone` observable and updates the transition to only take 1 emit'). The ground truth correctly identifies the faulty line, the complete-vs-unsubscribe semantics, the downstream consequence, and both parts of the fix. A reviewer can see the removal of `complete()` directly in the diff, but understanding why it matters requires knowing that the navigation transition waits on `bootstrapDone` completion, hence 'partly'.

The change adds the skip condition `if (part.match(_placeholderRe) && selector[res.index + 1]?.match(/[a-fA-F\d]/)) { continue; }` inside the selector-splitting loop, where `_placeholderRe` is `/__ph-(\d+)__/g`. That placeholder is the generic one SafeSelector emits for attribute selectors, `:nth-child(...)` content and escape sequences alike (the diff itself shows `restore()` using the same regex to restore all placeholders). So for a minified selector such as `:host[foo]>div`, the part before `>` contains `__ph-0__` (from `[foo]`) and the character after `>` is `d`, a hex digit, so the combinator is wrongly dropped and the selector is mis-scoped. With spaces present the char after the separator is whitespace, which is why only prod/minified builds broke — matching the fix message. The fix introduces a distinct `__esc-ph-N__` placeholder for `(\\.)` escapes and checks only that in the skip condition, with `restore` accepting both forms. The ground truth describes faulty code, mechanism and fix correctly. A reviewer could suspect the overreach from the diff (the same regex is used in `restore`), but confirming that attribute selectors share the placeholder requires reading SafeSelector's constructor outside the diff, hence 'partly'.

The change itself replaces the guarded calls in test_hooks.ts — `if (_global.beforeEach) { _global.beforeEach(getCleanupHook(false)); }` and the matching `afterEach` guard — with bare `beforeEach(getCleanupHook(false));` / `afterEach(getCleanupHook(true));`. If this module is evaluated where no test runner has defined those globals (e.g. it ends up in an app bundle), the bare identifier lookup throws a ReferenceError at module load. The fix restores the guard with `globalThis.beforeEach?.(...)` / `globalThis.afterEach?.(...)`, and its comment explicitly says the guard is needed because the file can make it into a bundle. The ground truth matches the code, mechanism and fix; the regression is visible directly in the diff since the removal of an explicit guard is the whole hunk.

The change adds an `isDefaultImport: false` field to each per-defer-block dependency (with the comment that it 'will be added later during the `compile` step'), and in `collectDeferredSymbols` it sets `deferBlockDep.isDeferrable = true` and `deferBlockDep.importPath = ...` but only writes `isDefaultImport: isDefaultImport(importDecl)` into the separate `deferrableTypes` map, never onto `deferBlockDep`. The same PR makes the defer-block loader generators (`template.ts` and `create_defer_deps_fns.ts`) read `deferredDep.isDefaultImport` / `dep.isDefaultImport`, which therefore stays `false`, so the per-block deps function emits `m.CmpA` instead of `m.default` for a default-imported component. The `setClassMetadataAsync` path uses the map and was correct, which is why the PR's `toContain('m => m.default')` test didn't catch it, as the fix message explains. The fix adds exactly `deferBlockDep.isDefaultImport = isDefaultImport(importDecl);`. The ground truth matches the faulty code, mechanism, and fix. All relevant pieces (the `false` initializer, the missing assignment in `collectDeferredSymbols`, and the readers of the flag) are in the diff, so a careful reviewer could spot it from the change alone.

The change adds `copyEventListenerOptions`, which replaces the caller's options object with `const newOptions: any = {...options};` and then only patches back `signal` (`if (options.signal) { newOptions.signal = options.signal; }`). Before this change the (non-passive-event) path handed the caller's own object to the native `addEventListener`, which reads each dictionary member with [[Get]], so getters, prototype properties and non-enumerable properties worked. After the change, only own enumerable data properties survive the spread, so `capture`/`once`/`passive` defined via `Object.defineProperty` or inherited from a prototype are dropped — exactly what the ground truth describes. The fix confirms this mechanism: it loops over `['capture', 'once', 'passive', 'signal']` and does `if (!Object.hasOwn(newOptions, key) && key in options) newOptions[key] = options[key];`. The defect is squarely in the added code, and a careful reviewer could spot it from the diff alone — the PR's own comment admits that spreading `{...options}` wouldn't copy the `signal` getter, which invites the question of why the same isn't true for the other members. One small nuance not worth downgrading: the canonical MDN passive feature test passes `null` as the listener, and `makeAddListener` short-circuits `if (!delegate) return nativeListener.apply(this, arguments)` before copying, so that exact snippet would not hit the bug; variants that pass a real function (common in libraries) would. The ground truth does not mention the fix's secondary reordering of `buildEventListenerOptions(copyEventListenerOptions(...))`, but that is incidental.

The change replaces `data.handleId = setNative!.apply(window, data.args)` with a branch that, when the native return value is not a number, runs `data.isRefreshable = isFunction(handleOrId.refresh);`. If a wrapped `setTimeout`/`setInterval`/`requestAnimationFrame` returns null or undefined (the change itself deletes the old comment 'some polyfill or browser may return undefined from setTimeout/...' and the guard `handle && handle.ref && ...` that tolerated it), the property access on null throws a TypeError synchronously. The fix commit changes exactly that line to `isFunction(handleOrId?.refresh)`, treating a nullish handle as non-refreshable. The ground truth correctly identifies the faulty line, the mechanism (unguarded property read on a nullish handle), the prior tolerance, and the fix. A reviewer could spot this from the diff alone since the removed comment and guard are visible right in the change.

Before the change, `_scopeSelector` split on every comma (`.split(/ ?, ?/)`), so a selector like `.foo:is(.a,
.b)` became `.foo:is(.a` and `
.b)`; the leading-newline part was fully consumed by `[^:]*` and nothing was dropped (output was wrong in other ways, but not truncated). The change introduced `selectorSplitRe` and a new `sep` regex that deliberately do not split inside parentheses, so `.foo:is(.a,
.b)` now reaches `_scopeSelectorPart` whole. There, `t.match(/([^:]*)(:*)(.*)/)` (pre-existing non-host branch) and the newly added `scopedP.match(/([^:]*)(:*)(.*)/)` use `.*`, which stops at the newline, yielding `.foo[contenta]:is(.a,` and losing the rest of the selector. The fix changes both trailing groups to `([\s\S]*)`, exactly as the ground truth says. The non-host regex itself predates the change, but the change is what makes newline-containing parts reach it in realistic multiline CSS, so attributing it to this change is fair. A reviewer could see the new `.*` regex and the new paren-preserving splits in the diff, but the main failing branch's regex is outside the shown hunk, hence 'partly'.

The change replaces the unconditional `metadata.dependencies = getDependenciesForDirective(...)` with `if (injector) { metadata.dependencies = ... }`, and makes `getInjectorFromElementNode` return `null` when `ng.getInjector` is absent (`ngDebugClient().getInjector?.(element) ?? null`). So on apps whose global `ng` lacks `getInjector`, `dependencies` is now left undefined where it was always set before. The DevTools template reads `controller().directiveMetadata?.dependencies.length > 0`; the safe-navigation only guards `directiveMetadata`, so `.length` on an undefined `dependencies` throws, exactly as the fix message says. The fix adds `@let dependencies = ...; @if (dependencies && dependencies.length > 0)`. The ground truth matches the faulty code, the mechanism and the fix. A reviewer could notice the new conditional assignment in the diff, but would need to know the consuming template outside the diff to see the crash, hence 'partly'.

Before the change, every anchor RouterLink subscribed unconditionally: `if (this.isAnchorElement) { this.subscription = router.events.subscribe(... NavigationEnd -> updateHref) }`. The change replaces this with `subscribeToNavigationEventsIfNecessary()`, which only subscribes when `preserveFragment`, or `queryParamsHandling` is 'merge'/'preserve', or the (oddly inverted) default-handling clause `!this.queryParamsHandling && !dependsOnRouterState(this.options?.defaultQueryParamsHandling)` holds. So a link like `[routerLink]="['./child']" queryParamsHandling="replace"` never subscribes, yet its href is resolved against the current ActivatedRoute and goes stale after navigation. The fix commit says exactly this ("its link can change when navigations cause the ActivatedRoute paths to change") and removes the condition so anchors always subscribe (`if (this.subscription !== undefined) return;` then subscribe), i.e. a rollback. The ground truth matches the faulty code, mechanism and fix, and sensibly warns that reporting only the inverted default clause would point toward fewer subscriptions, the opposite of the real fix. The defect is in the diff (the new conditional replaces an unconditional subscription), but recognizing why it is wrong requires knowing that `urlTree` is computed relative to the ActivatedRoute, which is outside the diff, hence 'partly'.

The change is the regression the fix message cites (#61241). It does two things that together cause the failure: (1) in `injector-tree.component.ts` it replaces the message-bus-driven update with an `afterRenderEffect` that, on every `componentExplorerView` change, runs `this.init()` and `untracked(() => this.updateInjectorTreeVisualization(view.forest))` with no visibility check; (2) in `devtools-tabs` it switches to `[hidden]="!injectorTreeVisible"` and deletes the special rule `ng-injector-tree.hidden { display: block; visibility: hidden; position: absolute; }` that previously kept the injector tree laid out while off-screen. So after the tab has been opened and the user switches away, D3 keeps re-laying-out/translating SVGs inside a `display:none` element, producing the 'translate' errors the fix message describes. The fix matches the ground truth exactly: it adds `hidden = input<boolean>(false)` bound via `host: {'[hidden]': 'hidden()'}`, returns early with `|| untracked(this.hidden)`, and guards `init()` with `if (!this.isInitialized)` so the listener/visualizers aren't recreated each run. The ground truth's description of the faulty code, mechanism and fix is accurate; the additional `snapToNode` null check in the fix is a separate extra not claimed by the label. A reviewer could spot the problem from the diff alone, since the deleted CSS rule explicitly shows the component needed layout while hidden and the new effect visibly re-runs `init()` every time.

The change replaces `"@npm//:node_modules/zone.js/bundles/zone.umd.min.js"` with `"//:node_modules/zone.js"` in `devtools/src/BUILD.bazel` (the `devapp` pkg_web) and in `devtools/projects/shell-browser/src/BUILD.bazel`, which relocates the packaged file from `./npm/node_modules/...` to `./node_modules/...`. The change itself demonstrates this by updating `demo-standalone/src/index.html` from `./npm/node_modules/zone.js/...` to `./node_modules/zone.js/...`, but it does not make the same edit to `devtools/src/index.html` or `devtools/projects/shell-browser/src/index.html`, which the fix commit does (`-<script src="./npm/node_modules/zone.js/bundles/zone.umd.min.js">` -> `+<script src="./node_modules/zone.js/bundles/zone.umd.min.js">`). The fix message explicitly calls this a regression from the change (#62083). The ground truth correctly identifies the faulty BUILD edits, the mechanism (stale script path, zone.js not loaded), and the fix. A reviewer could infer the inconsistency from the diff (demo-standalone's index.html updated, others not), but confirming it requires knowing the other two index.html files reference the old `./npm/` path, hence 'partly'.

The change replaces `.toPromise()` with a hand-rolled `firstValueFrom` that is implemented as `source.pipe(first()).subscribe(...)`. rxjs `first()` raises an `EmptyError` when the source completes without ever emitting, whereas `toPromise()` would simply resolve `undefined`. The change applies this new helper to `matchWithChecks`, `runCanLoadGuards` and `loadChildren` in `recognize.ts`, so any guard/matcher chain that completes empty now rejects with `EmptyError`. The recognizer's retry loop only swallows `NoMatch` (`if (e?.name === NO_MATCH_ERROR_NAME) { continue; }`), so the EmptyError propagates and the navigation fails rather than trying the next route. The fix commit confirms this ("This fixes a bug introduced in #63485 where `firstValueFrom` was used ... some observables don't emit before completing") and the fix diff adds `|| isEmptyError(e)` to that catch, exactly as the ground truth states. The ground truth's claim about how `toPromise()`'s `undefined` result was handled before is slightly hand-wavy, but the faulty code, the mechanism (EmptyError not caught) and the fix are all described correctly. A reviewer could notice the `first()` vs `toPromise()` empty-completion difference from the diff itself, but would need to know the catch block in `recognize.ts` (outside the diff) only handles `NoMatch` to see the consequence, hence "partly".

The change rewrites `cancelLeavingNodes` and adds a new removal condition: `(leavingParent && newParent && leavingParent !== newParent)`. Previously the function only cancelled a leaving element when it was the exact node before the insertion point (`leavingEl === previousNode`); now any element tracked under the same TNode that lives in a different DOM parent is immediately given a cancelling `animationend` event and removed via `leavingEl.parentNode?.removeChild(leavingEl)`. Because `leavingNodes` is keyed by TNode (shared by every instance of a template), two independent sibling instances in separate parents (accordion sections, nav panels) also satisfy 'different parent', so the leaving sibling's `animate.leave` is skipped. The fix keeps the sibling-check branch but gates the cross-parent branch on `newDeclarationView === leavingDeclarationView` (tracked via `trackLeavingNodes(..., parentLView)`), exactly as the ground truth says. The defect is wholly within the added code, and a reviewer reading the diff's own comment ('In a different DOM parent (overlay/portal case...)') versus the much broader actual condition could spot that it over-matches.

The change replaces `'${position}'` (which implicitly stringifies an array as "0,1,2") with `stringifyAndEscape(position)` = `JSON.stringify(JSON.stringify(obj))`, so the inspected page now receives the string "[0,1,2]". The backend consumer `findNodeFromSerializedPosition` still did `serializedPosition.split(',').map((index) => parseInt(index, 10))`, which yields NaN for "[0" and "2]", breaking view-source and select-DOM-element. The fix changes the backend to `JSON.parse(serializedPosition)`, matching the fix message about a regression from the comma-separated to JSON array format. The ground truth correctly describes the faulty code, the mechanism and the fix. A reviewer can see the wire format change in the diff, but needs to know the backend's parsing in component-tree.ts (outside the diff) to realize it breaks, hence 'partly'.
